script: Scientists can sometimes tell what color a dinosaur was. They look for melanosomes, tiny pigment structures preserved in fossil feathers. Their shapes hint at colors like black, brown, gray or ginger. Sinosauropteryx had a striped tail with ginger and white bands. It also seems to have had a dark mask across its eyes, like a raccoon. Bright blues and greens from other pigments are much harder to detect. Follow DinoBytes for more prehistoric facts.
